explanation: I run a small construction subcontracting firm. Our two main contractors pay us by cheque for completed work. We pay our seven regular suppliers and crew out of that: materials by cheque and card, the equipment lease by wire, and site wages in cash. Almost everything that comes in goes out on costs within the month. I can share both contracts and the supplier invoices.
rationale: 2 payers, 7 payees, formats and near-total pass-through all match

explanation: This is the operating account of my export business and it holds our working capital from earlier sales. Two distributors pay us by cheque every few days, and we pay our four suppliers by cheque, ACH, wire and card as soon as goods are dispatched, so cheques that come in are often paid out again within a day. Our statements for the past year show the same cycle.
rationale: 2 payers, 4 payees, fast forwarding; outflow above inflow explained by existing working capital

explanation: In August I sold my family's commercial property and the buyer's bank sent one transfer of USD 1,835,585 (sale deed attached). Since then I have been paying renovation contractors and furniture and appliance shops for our new home by cheque and card, which is why there are many small payments to different shops.
rationale: single large inflow matching the amount, many small payments to 16 payees

explanation: I am a wholesale electronics dealer. My three retail customers pay small amounts by card and cheque during the week. I pay my three suppliers by cheque, card and cash as soon as stock arrives, mostly from the balance built up over the previous quarter. Large cheques and cash payments to suppliers are normal in this trade. GST returns attached.
rationale: 3 payers, 3 payees, formats match; large outflows from existing balance

explanation: This is our company's treasury account. Two small subsidiaries pay intra-group charges into it by card and cheque. The large ACH and cheque payments out are the scheduled settlement of our term loan and payments to four vendors, funded from reserves that were already in the account at the start of the month. Board resolution and loan schedule attached.
rationale: 2 payers, 5 payees incl. one very large ACH payee; huge outflow needs the reserves claim, which the data cannot contradict

explanation: I pay my shop landlord twice a week by cheque and card for rent and shared stock, always the same two amounts. The money comes from my savings already in this account. The two small ACH credits of USD 300.05 are interest from my fixed deposit.
rationale: 1 payee, repeated identical amounts, 2 small credits of 300.05

explanation: After a fire at our factory, the insurer paid our claim settlement of USD 4,657,537 by cheque. Since then we have been paying contractors, equipment sellers and our staff's medical bills by card and cheque as we rebuild, about a dozen different payees.
rationale: single cheque matching the amount, 12 payees, small card and cheque payments

explanation: My employer reimbursed my travel expenses twice. My regular payments go to two places only, my children's school and my housing finance company, by cheque, card and ACH, from savings already in the account.
rationale: 1 payer with 2 credits, exactly 2 payees, formats match

explanation: I sold my old phone online and the buyer paid me. The rest is money my friends sent me.
rationale: 19 credits from 4 senders, onward transfers and 8 cycles unexplained

explanation: These two credits were my salary and a bonus. The next morning I paid my rent.
rationale: 2 different senders, 2 payees including a large yen transfer, outflow larger than inflow, link to a reported account unexplained

explanation: I run tuition classes and the parents pay me the fees.
rationale: 14 senders plausible, but onward transfers to 8 receivers and the reported-account link are unexplained

explanation: A friend's account was blocked, so he sent money to me and I paid his suppliers for him. I did not keep anything.
rationale: admits the account was used on behalf of another person (the SOP's definition of a mule account)

explanation: I am a freelance graphic designer and these are payments from my clients.
rationale: does not explain sending 98% on to 2 receivers, nor the reported-account link

explanation: These were gifts from my relatives for my wedding.
rationale: outflows of over USD 117 million to 16 receivers are not explained by wedding gifts

explanation: I work for a payroll company and pay its employees' salaries from my personal account on the company's behalf.
rationale: personal account used on behalf of another party; 20 payees, cash and cheque inflows, reported-account link
